description: We are Savanna Orbit, creators of Kaka-to-Bazara (www.kakatobazara.earth)—a live app using NASA satellite data and AI to help Nigerian farmers unlock post-harvest soil moisture. We bring skills in NASA APIs, GIS mapping, Gemini AI, and web dev. Since our app is already live, you'll help elevate a working prototype! Looking for UI/UX designers, agri-experts, and storytellers to polish our demo and pitch. Join us to make the savanna bloom!
summary:
Kaka-to-Bazara is a live, mobile-first agricultural decision-support web application built by team Savanna Orbit to help smallholder farmers across Gombe State and Nigeria unlock hidden post-harvest soil moisture for dry-season farming.

Addressing the Field Shift challenge, our platform bridges the gap between complex Earth observation portals and rural farmers. Users tap their exact farmland on a labeled hybrid satellite map—or search nationwide via our Nigeria Crop Finder—to inspect real-time NASA POWER root-zone soil wetness, rainfall, temperature, NASA GIBS (SMAP & MODIS) vegetation layers, and 30m SRTM terrain drainage. An integrated Gemini AI advisor translates these metrics into plain-language crop viability verdicts and 3-option rotation plans in English, Hausa, Fulfulde, and Nigerian Pidgin.

By turning invisible satellite moisture data into actionable planting advice without costly irrigation fuel, Kaka-to-Bazara prevents topsoil erosion, restores soil nitrogen, and enables a profitable second harvest during Nigeria’s six-month dry season.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Kaka-to-Bazara (www.kakatobazara.earth) is a live, mobile-first agricultural decision-support web application designed to help smallholder farmers across Gombe State and Nigeria unlock hidden post-harvest soil moisture for dry-season farming. In Hausa, Kaka refers to the main October harvest, and Bazara refers to the hot, dry season that follows.

The platform works through two core modules:

  1. My Farm Checker (Plot-Level Soil & Rotation Analysis): Farmers select one of Gombe State’s 11 Local Government Areas (or tap any exact coordinate on a labeled hybrid satellite map) and adjust their farm size in hectares and soil texture (Sandy, Loamy, or Clay). The app fetches live NASA POWER agroclimatology data—root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT), rainfall (PRECTOTCORR), maximum temperature (T2M_MAX), and evapotranspiration (EVPTRNS)—alongside 30-meter SRTM elevation to estimate remaining days of usable underground moisture. Farmers can toggle NASA GIBS satellite layers (MODIS NDVI vegetation and SMAP soil moisture) and receive an instant viability verdict on whether their planned crop will succeed or fail.
  2. Nigeria Crop Finder (Nationwide Scaling): Farmers across all 36 Nigerian states can select or type any crop to view optimal planting and harvest windows, key dry-season risks, and the top-ranked agro-ecological basins in Nigeria with one-tap satellite inspection.
  3. Multilingual AI Crop & Rotation Advisor: Powered by Google Gemini AI, the app compares 3 practical rotation paths (Bare Fallow vs. 60-Day Drought-Hardy Cowpea vs. Fodder Lablab) and lets farmers ask follow-up questions in English, Hausa, Fulfulde, or Nigerian Pidgin.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Zero-Fuel Dry-Season Harvests: Most smallholder farmers leave fields bare for six months after harvest because they cannot afford fuel-powered irrigation pumps. Kaka-to-Bazara identifies residual moisture already trapped in the root zone, enabling a profitable bonus harvest without fuel costs.
  • Soil Conservation & Nitrogen Restoration: Instead of leaving topsoil exposed to Harmattan wind erosion and extreme heat, recommending short-cycle nitrogen-fixing legumes (like cowpea and lablab) protects soil structure, reduces dust, and naturally enriches the land before the next rainy season.
  • Accessible Space Science: By translating raw satellite indices into plain-language verdicts across four local languages, Kaka-to-Bazara puts NASA Earth observation data directly into the hands of everyday farmers and agricultural extension workers.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend & Mapping: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Leaflet.js with Esri World Imagery, place/road name overlays, and Nominatim reverse geocoding.
  • NASA & Scientific Data Sources: NASA POWER API (daily root-zone soil wetness, precipitation, temperature, evapotranspiration), NASA GIBS (MODIS Terra NDVI and SMAP soil moisture layers), SRTM 30m Digital Elevation Model, and FAO GAEZ crop water thresholds.
  • AI & Localization: Google Gemini AI (@google/genai) with custom agronomic system instructions supporting English, Hausa, Fulfulde, and Nigerian Pidgin.
  • Deployment & Hosting: GitHub for version control and Vercel for continuous cloud hosting on the custom domain www.kakatobazara.earth.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

  • Bridging Space Data with Ground Realities: Satellites measure regional moisture and terrain, but cannot see below-surface hardpan, local land tenure, or open dry-season livestock grazing. We creatively designed our AI advisor to explicitly combine satellite metrics with practical on-the-ground reminders (such as checking soil compaction and fencing against open grazing).
  • Terrain-Aware Hydrology: We accounted for the sharp contrast between low-lying river basins (Fadama lowlands like Yamaltu-Deba/Dadinkowa, which retain moisture longer) and fast-draining sandy uplands.
  • Low-Bandwidth & Non-Technical UX: Designed with a clean 3-step onboarding flow, clear visual badges, and local language switching so any farmer or extension agent can get an actionable recommendation in under 30 seconds on a standard smartphone.
